findings: Guardian initially consumed an application breakpoint as its own attach stop; recovery now never treats it as an initial stop.
Three post-fix breakpoint runs failed an incorrect harness expectation. Undebugged baselines then showed native exit 0x80000003; corrected harness preserves it.
90-case run had one concurrent cancellation failure; its short stderr tail did not identify the worker exception.
Rapid cancellation reproduced two worker single-step failures in five runs, correlated with frozen DR6.B0/RIP entry before event publication.
Disable-then-thaw first revision still failed. Later diagnostics identified own_slot_missing, with disabled debug registers zero at event delivery.
Final cleanup retains an already-triggered owned slot until its actual event, then sets RF, clears the slot and continues before detach.
First expanded108 had105 pass and3 cancellation-semantics failures: guardian polling lagged behind200 hits; all3 targets resumed.
Final owner checks guardian process identity on every event-loop iteration; targeted5 and final108 passed.
teardown_caveat: For cleanup:unknown cases the target was still alive before test teardown. Single-step after killing both test debugger roles is not evidence of successful normal recovery or the original error cause.
